newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA SEEN FACING SLUMPING MEAT PRODUCTION.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA SEEN FACING SLUMPING MEAT PRODUCTION.

text.p: Bulgaria's Agriculture Ministry said on Tuesday it expected meat production to fall but did not plan imports to fill the gap.
"In 1997 local production is expected at 270,000 tonnes of meat, down by 45,000 tonnes in 1996," Deputy Agriculture Minister Dimo Uzunov told a news conference.
"Although fodder prices are high, I think local producers will be able to meet the country's meat needs," he said.
Uzunov denied that there would be pork shortages because of unprecedented slaughter of pigs in the wake of this year's poor grain harvest.
Pork production is seen falling to 150,000 tonnes in 1996 from 257,500 tonnes in 1995. It is expected to fall further to 128,000 tonnes in 1997 .
The ministry's forecasts for goats' meat and mutton are expected to be 32,800 tonnes this year against 45,000 tonnes last year. The ministry expects meat production of 24,340 tonnes in 1997.
This year's beef production is estimated at 50,900 tonnes while next year it is expected to fall to 48,100 tonnes. It was 70,652 tonnes in 1995.
Chicken meat production is expected to fall to 81,000 tonnes this year from 97,000 tonnes in 1995. It is expected to fall to 79,000 tonnes in 1997.

Annual meat consumption in 1995 was 61 kg per capita, while the expected demand for this year and 1997 is 40 kg per capita, officials said, adding that the country's economic crisis meant demand would be lower.
Bulgaria, in the throes of a grave grain crisis caused by excessive exports last year and poor harvest this year, intends to import large quantities of grain and fodder.
